correctness.rationale: A direct induction on Heyting terms proves local-level and zero-signature necessity. Negation and double negation isolate every coordinate when signatures are injective, and the local entries supply each intermediate level; coordinatewise joins suffice. Distinct decorated signatures give the coefficient formula and sharp minimum. For the probability law, pair coincidences have probability q^r and v-fold coincidence t_v^r with t_v<q^(v/2) for v>2; the Poisson factorial-moment and large-mean second-moment arguments are valid. The missing-level event is bounded by (k-2)n p^r and is negligible in bounded-collision regimes. All endpoints k=2, n=1, r=0 are covered. Independent direct finite closure code was actually executed on 11,189 tuples, 36 census parameter triples, and 693 rank checks; experiments are corroboration, not a proof of the infinite claims.

value.rationale: The complete exact enumeration and natural rank of generators for powers of finite Heyting chains quantify finite generation in an algebraic logic signature. The criterion separates two mathematically distinct obstructions (indistinguishable zero signatures and absent local intermediate values), and the biased birthday law gives a genuinely different typical threshold from the sharp deterministic rank. The finite-power comparison to distributive-lattice reducts is motivated by the mathematical effect of implication, not by an arbitrary finite computation.
